0.long_answer: The glaucoma in question is the juvenile open‐angle form, which is uncommon overall but has been noted in some patients with Ackerman syndrome. This particular type of glaucoma typically follows an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance. It usually manifests early in life and is inherited in families where a parent has the condition. In the context of Ackerman syndrome—an already rare familial condition with distinctive dental and other manifestations—the occasional occurrence of juvenile open‐angle glaucoma aligns with the syndrome’s genetic background and clinical variability.
